intro: Paluma is remote walking country. Phone reception is unreliable, weather changes quickly and help can take hours to reach you. The offline map works without a signal; your battery, water and a plan are what you rely on.

emergency.headline: In an emergency, call 000. On a mobile, 112 connects to the same emergency service.
steps: Do not send an SMS directly to 000 or 112; these numbers do not receive text messages.
Give your coordinates from this screen and the number of the nearest junction.
Say how many people are with you and what the injury or hazard is.
Stay where you are if it is safe to do so, keep warm and dry, and make yourself easy to find.
For a call over a mobile network, coverage from at least one provider is needed. Dialling 112 does not create reception where no mobile network is available.
If a call cannot connect, keep yourself safe and seek help from people nearby or another available way to contact emergency services.

sections.title: Before you set out
items: Tell someone where you are going, which junctions you plan to pass and when you expect to be back.
Carry a paper map, a charged phone and a power bank. Download the offline map before leaving reception.
Check the forecast and park alerts. Tracks can close after heavy rain or for planned burns.
Walking times in this app are estimates only. They assume a steady pace without breaks and do not include elevation.

sections.title: Water and heat
items: Carry more water than you expect to need, and treat creek water before drinking it.
Start early. Exposed sections and the climbs out of the creeks get hot through the middle of the day.
Turn back if you are behind your plan, the weather turns, or someone in the group is struggling.

sections.title: Wildlife and plants
items: Leeches and ticks are common after rain. Check yourself, your clothing and your pack at the end of the walk.
Snakes may rest on or beside the track. Give them room and look before stepping over logs.
Stinging trees and wait-a-while grow close to some tracks. Long trousers and care with your hands help.

sections.title: Reception and navigation
items: Reception is patchy on the plateau and often absent in the gullies and below the range.
GPS accuracy drops under dense canopy. Compare the map with track markers and junction numbers.
If you leave the track, stop and return to the last place where you were sure of your position.
